newsitem.title: USA: Casas - Venezuela will try to restrict money - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Casas - Venezuela will try to restrict money - RFTV.

text.p: The Venezuelan central bank would continue with its restrictive monetary policy to keep inflation down in the face of wage increases, Central Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez said.
Casas said increases in salaries were necessary in Venezuela from a social point of view although the excess liquidity was worrying.
"..It worries me, especially as head of the central bank," Casas told Reuters Financial Television in an interview recorded Sunday and aired on Monday.
Wage increases would have some benefits in reactivating consumption among the middle and lower classes.
"The central bank will have to go on with a very restrictive policy," Casas said, although he added that the bank was lacking the instruments to run even tighter monetary policy.
"Inflation has gone down and has been one of the big successes," Casas said, down from 12.5 percent monthly in May of 1996 to 1.6 percent in March.
"The problem is to maintain inflation within a manageable level and in order to do that we have to cut down the excess liquidity."

Casas said Venezuela would try to keep inflation as low as possible but, "we are not probably going to hit the (25 percent) target that we had set out at the beginning of the year, but it will never go back this year to the levels of inflation we had last year."
